title: BMW F 450 GS Review | The littlest GS is an absolute ripper - MCNews
content:
The lightweight adventure bike market has been one of the hottest segments in recent years, for good reason. Compared to ‘full-size’ bikes, options around the 450 cc mark are lighter, easier to ride, more forgiving, more nimble and, crucially for many of us, cheaper to buy, run and repair. Most of the recent noise has come from China (CFMOTO’s 450MT), India (Royal Enfield’s Himalayan 450), Austria/India (KTM’s 390 Adventure R) and, more recently, Japan/Thailand (Kawasaki’s KLE500). All are worthy prospects, each with their own strengths, and some will appeal more than others depending on riding and styling preferences. You could argue that a few other bikes are in the mix too, but these are the models selling in volume, and it is a sign of the times that none are made in Europe, even if they have European badges on the tanks. Things are only heating up further, because now Germany, via their tie-up with Indian manufacturer TVS, has stepped up to the plate and is ready to play ball with the new F 450 GS. I’m not sure why I went with the baseball analogy (do they even play baseball in Germany? India?), but what I can tell you straight up… they’ve smacked it out of the park.  We believe the F 450 GS is built at the same TVS factory as the new Norton Atlas. Ever since the bike was first teased at EICMA in 2024, adventure riders have been waiting impatiently for the production version to land. MCNews finally got to sample the new bike at the Australian press launch in Victoria and put it through its paces on quality gravel roads, fire trails, and some tarmac. I might have even found a puddle or two for splashy splashy pics… First up, power-to-weight. Straight to the top of the class. Within a couple of kilograms of the KTM, with a touch more power and torque. That torque difference might not seem like much on paper, but it’s a massive difference once you’re on the bike. Power is shown in mechanical horsepower, with ratios calculated before rounding. We were told that 80 per cent of the torque is available from as low as 3,000 rpm, and that’s how it feels. The littlest GS will lift the front wheel in second gear without the clutch and is easily the gruntiest-feeling engine in the class. It’s an absolute ripper. It’s actually a 420 cc parallel twin, one with a unique 135-degree crankpin offset that results in an uneven firing order and a terrific exhaust note. Methinks there’s a bit of a hooligan hidden away in there, wanting to be unleashed… The sound of one winding out, even with the stock pipe, is properly encouraging. While it’s a short-stroke design, with a bore diameter of 72 mm and a stroke length of 51.6 mm, it doesn’t rely on revs to make power as that oversquare ratio might suggest. Power delivery is beautifully smooth from idle through to redline. It runs a 13:1 compression ratio, which is reasonably high (and explains the solid performance numbers), and it’s designed to run on 95 RON fuel. Something to keep in mind when planning remote trips. Throttle feel is excellent, fuelling is spot on, and that quickshifter completes what I reckon is the best engine and gearbox package in the class. It’s a solid step ahead of everything else, which is not what I expected. With 180 mm of suspension travel, it has the most gravel-road-focussed spec in the class, with the KTM the most off-road-focused at 230 mm. It’s not as straightforward as you might expect, though, as they’ve managed to give the bike a healthy 220 mm of ground clearance, which is pretty much in line with the CFMOTO and Royal Enfield. Likewise, the seat height and fuel range are around mid-pack. In fact, it’s probably easier to point to the outliers for differentiation here. The Himi gets the most range, the KTM the most suspension travel and the Kawi the lowest ground clearance. Here’s how it stacks up against the other bikes. But here’s where the numbers don’t tell the full story. Even on the 4WD trails, on standard settings, there was no suggestion that the suspension wasn’t enough. Unless you’re expecting to tackle big hits at speed or do decent jumps over water bars, this setup will likely do the job for most riders. Yes, it will bottom out on jumps on standard settings, but I don’t think it’s been designed with that in mind. The best way I can illustrate how well the launch bikes performed on the trail is to point out how surprised I was to see the 180 mm number when I started writing this review. If you’re on the fence due to that spec alone, I’d suggest you try to get a test ride. You might be surprised… The other thing you can’t see from those tables above is arguably the second of three big selling points for the GS after power-to-weight. That’s build quality and standard tech. The BMW absolutely shines here, with a quick-shifter, heated grips, rider modes, and adjustable TC and ABS (on the fly!) all standard on the Sport or Trophy variants, which pretty much everyone chooses. It’s easily the most premium-feeling offering in the segment, with the only thing absent from a tech perspective being cruise control, which sadly isn’t an option. Only the KTM gets that as an option. The Beemer also gets some seriously good-quality switchgear and a 6.5-inch TFT dash, the same hardware and menu system used on the 450’s bigger siblings. It’s a nice touch, a clever way of introducing potential new customers to the GS experience. The third major selling point is how usable the bike is for riders of all experience levels. And I’d group three aspects of the bike into the usability bucket. Let’s start with what BMW are calling their Easy Ride Clutch. A centrifugal setup not unlike a Rekluse for those who’ve used them before. Essentially, it’s a twist-and-go affair, which is especially helpful when picking your way between rocks or trees, or making tight turns on the trail. Crucially, it still has engine braking when decelerating, so if you picture yourself rolling down a 4WD track, you can still count on that to help keep things tidy without always needing to ride the rear brake. With the excellent quickshifter, once on the move, you don’t actually have to touch the clutch at all. For experienced riders who are used to using the clutch and might be worried about losing specific clutch techniques, you can still give the clutch a dip if you want to dial up some more revs for an obstacle or to lift the front, for example. It just has a slightly different feel. In action, once first gear is engaged (using the clutch) and the clutch lever is released, the bike remains sitting still until you dial up the revs. On the launch bike, the clutch felt like it didn’t start engaging until just under 3,000 rpm, which seemed a little high to me at first. But more time on the bike had me getting more comfortable with it. Personally, I’d still prefer the regular clutch, mostly from muscle memory, but the easy clutch has some drawbacks. You do lose the ability to use the clutch as a handbrake with the engine switched off, for instance. That said, I suspect if I rode one on and off for a few weeks, it would become second nature. Interestingly, the top-spec Trophy variant is only available with the easy clutch. Which surprises me. It means you’d have to spec up the Sport variant with all of the added extras that the Trophy gets if you want the full experience but with a regular clutch. So you’d miss out on that lovely Trophy colour scheme! The two other aspects of the bike that greatly impact ease of riding are seat height and steering lock. The seat height is a relatively obvious one. It feels lower than the 845 mm spec sheet suggests. At 181 cm, I could comfortably put both feet flat on the ground. That’s a huge confidence booster when moving the bike around at low speed or picking your way around obstacles on the trail. Throwing a foot out for a quick dab becomes child’s play in tight turns. Speaking of tight turns, that’s where the steering lock comes in. It has to be up there with the best on any bike I’ve ridden, allowing you to turn the bike around in a seemingly impossible space. So when you add the easy clutch, low seat height and super-tight steering lock together, doing spin turns on narrow trails becomes something to look forward to, not something to plan out because you’re on a big, heavy bike. Brakes are excellent. A single 310 mm disc on the front employs a four-piston monoblock Brembo caliper, and the rear is also from the Brembo family. It runs a ByBre single-piston caliper on a 240 mm disc. ByBre is Brembo’s wholly owned Indian brand (and short for ‘By Brembo’). I found the rear to have more than decent feel, and I never felt the front was underpowered. In Enduro Pro mode, with the front ABS set to its most off-road setting and the rear ABS deactivated, I was perfectly happy. It comes with cast wheels as standard, in the more road/gravel-focused sizes of 19-inch front and 17-inch rear rather than a 21-inch front. Spoked wheels add about $1,500, and almost all customers are opting for them, according to the team from BMW Australia. Now, there are a few contributing factors here. You might first assume they’ve been a bit cheeky to keep the base price down. But you also need to realise that Australia is a small market in the grand scheme of things, and one of only a handful of markets with such a big focus on off-road riding. Add in the fact that post-COVID (yes, we’re still normalising even now, can you believe it?) getting supplies of the spoked wheels in the volumes needed proved a challenge. So they would have rightly prioritised the highest demand first. Road/gravel spec, rather than off-road brawler enduro spec. Taking all of that into account, if I were to pull out my crystal ball and make a product strategy prediction, I’d guess an enduro spec might be in the pipeline in the next year or two, to be introduced just as the initial demand for this model starts to be met. Longer-travel suspension, more ground clearance, 21-inch front and 19-inch rear wheels? Oof. Wonder if we’ll see something like that at Red Bull Romaniacs…? Back to the task at hand. How do they perform? The lighter cast wheels are slightly more eager and agile on the tarmac, as expected, but I definitely preferred the spoked wheels when hitting off-road bumps and potholes and picking through rougher 4WD tracks. That little bit of extra weight adds some deflection control and stability amongst bumps and rocky terrain, and it still tips in just fine on tarmac. I would tick the spoked wheels option. To say I was surprised by the little GS is a massive understatement. This bike is seriously capable and playful like no other in the class. Dripping with quality. Solid tech. Easy to ride and oh-so-encouraging. But most importantly, it’s FUN. BMW have dropped two fun bikes in recent times. I was equally blown away by the R 12 G/S last year and ended up giving it my Off-Road Bike of the Year gong. And now we have this little weapon. This 450 GS is not a beginner’s bike. Labelling it as such would be massively underselling the bike’s capability and potential. It’s absolutely beginner-friendly, but you’d be underestimating the bike if you thought it was only for less experienced riders. There is plenty to enjoy here for riders of all capabilities. At the risk of labouring the point on how much ‘potential’ this bike has up its sleeve, I’d love to ride the BMW Safari Enduro on one. That would be a lot of fun. I think with some aggressive rubber and a couple of mods, the littlest GS could be an absolute hoot. The first shipment of 400 bikes has already been snapped up, with the next batch due in Q2 2027. Pricing sits at around $12,700 ride-away for the red Sport model and $13,300 for the BMW blue-white-and-red Trophy model that gets the easy clutch and aluminium bash plate. On top of that, you’ll want to add the spoked wheels, which are another $1,517. There’s a whole bunch of BMW accessories ready to go, as you’d imagine. The one to look for is the Rallye pack, which includes the Rally seat, bar risers, engine case protection, TFT protector, and a tank pad. That bundle adds $990 to the bill (instead of $1,225 if you bought the parts individually). If you opt for the standard clutch on the Sport model, you’ll also want to tick the aluminium bash plate option for another $381. So once you’ve ticked the spoked wheels and Rallye pack options, you’re sitting around the mid-15 grand mark. Certainly not the cheapest in the class… but I think this is a genuine case of getting what you pay for, and it comes with a class-leading five-year warranty. Wayne loves all things motorsport, but lives for two wheels. Mountain bikes, dirt bikes, adventure bikes, road bikes, race bikes, the lot.

The sheer size of the new class has drawn considerable attention from market observers and industry watchers, as it signals the areas where the bank sees its most significant growth avenues in the years ahead. The composition of the new partner class is notably tilted toward the bank's wealth and asset management divisions, reflecting a deliberate strategic shift that has been underway for several years. As a constituent of the S&P 500 and one of the most storied names in global finance, Goldman Sachs has historically been defined by its dominance in trading and dealmaking. Goldman Sachs has been steadily building out its wealth management platform, aiming to transform what was once a relatively modest part of the enterprise into a core pillar of the bank's earnings. The bank has been deploying considerable resources into technology, talent acquisition, and platform enhancements to serve a broader range of clients, from ultra-high-net-worth individuals and families to the emerging affluent segment. The expansion of the wealth management business is seen as a way to diversify the bank's revenue base and reduce its dependence on the more volatile trading and advisory businesses that have traditionally dominated the earnings mix. The strategic emphasis on wealth management also reflects broader trends in the financial services industry, where firms are increasingly competing for affluent clients and their associated asset pools. While the wealth management push has garnered significant attention, Goldman Sachs continues to operate one of the most formidable capital markets and dealmaking franchises in the world. The bank's advisory business has been active in an environment where corporate merger and acquisition activity has been gradually recovering from the slowdown experienced during the period of rapid interest rate increases. Goldman Sachs has maintained its position near the top of the league tables for advisory mandates, underwriting transactions, and structured finance deals. The trading business has also been a source of strength, with the equities and bond market desks capitalizing on periods of elevated volatility and increased client activity. Goldman Sachs has been a major participant in the growing market for structured products and derivatives, areas where the bank's quantitative expertise and willingness to commit capital set it apart from many competitors. The resilience of the capital markets franchise provides a strong complement to the more stable earnings expected from the expanding wealth management operations, creating a more balanced and diversified business model overall. Goldman Sachs has been at the forefront of the massive capital deployment required to build out the infrastructure underpinning the artificial intelligence revolution. The bank has been involved in structuring and distributing some of the largest financing packages in the technology sector, including landmark deals tied to AI chip procurement and data center construction. These transactions represent a new and rapidly growing area of activity for the bank's structured finance and syndicated lending teams, and they have positioned Goldman Sachs as a go-to intermediary for companies seeking to finance enormous capital expenditure programs associated with the AI buildout. The scale of AI-related financing activity has been remarkable, reflecting the enormous sums that technology companies are committing to secure computing capacity and semiconductor supply. For Goldman Sachs, this wave of financing activity represents a convergence of several of the bank's core competencies, including its ability to structure complex transactions, its deep relationships with both technology companies and institutional capital providers, and its willingness to deploy balance sheet resources to facilitate large deals. Goldman Sachs' asset management division has been undergoing its own transformation, with the bank streamlining its operations and focusing on higher-margin strategies in alternatives, private credit, and real estate. The firm has been raising substantial capital for its private equity, infrastructure, and credit funds, tapping into strong institutional demand for alternative strategies in an environment where traditional bond and equity portfolios face elevated uncertainty. The asset management business provides durable fee-based revenue that complements the more transaction-dependent earnings of the capital markets divisions. The strategic alignment between the wealth management and asset management platforms is a key element of Goldman Sachs' broader evolution. By channeling the wealth management clients' assets into proprietary and externally managed strategies, the bank can deepen relationships and capture a greater portion of the value chain. title: Will the UK Economy Beat Expectations Again in 2027? - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. The UK economy faces a series of headwinds in the coming months after outperforming economists’ expectations in 2026. But Goldman Sachs Research expects GDP growth to accelerate again in late 2027, boosted by strong investment, improving productivity, and declining energy prices, producing another year of above-consensus growth. Our economists forecast that UK real GDP will grow 1.4% in 2027 (fourth quarter over fourth quarter). That’s down from an estimated 1.6% this year, but above the 1.2% consensus of economists’ expectations. “We see compelling reasons to be constructive on the economic outlook for 2027,” write Senior UK Economist James Moberly and Chief European Economist Jari Stehn. The UK economy proved “surprisingly resilient” in 2026, Moberly and Stehn write. Growth accelerated despite the energy shock keeping inflation elevated and causing the Bank of England to pivot from cutting to hiking. The labor market also showed signs of improvement, with unemployment falling and employment growth indicators ticking up. The new government also navigated a challenging fiscal backdrop to maintain its path of consolidation. “The coming quarters are likely to prove more challenging in several respects,” Moberly and Stehn write. They expect growth to slow in the near term, running slightly below trend in the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first half of 2027. The impact of the energy shock on household finances is likely to build over the winter, with weak real disposable income growth resulting in a slowdown in consumer spending. Our economists anticipate that rising inflation will push the BoE to hike rates by 25 basis points to 4.25%, probably in February. Tighter financial conditions should also weigh on growth as mortgages are refixed at higher rates. Fiscal policy is likely to have a more negative impact on economic growth in 2027 given that current plans imply a larger consolidation than in 2026. Our economists also see signs that the labor market could weaken gradually. They project that the unemployment rate will rise from 4.7% to 5% by the middle of 2027. “Despite these cyclical challenges, we see several reasons to be more constructive on the UK’s economic prospects for 2027,” Moberly and Stehn write. Some of the factors boosting growth in 2026 look like long-term advantages for the UK. Strong business investment has partly reflected rising capex in information and communications and in utilities, both of which look likely to continue. This should in turn support continued growth in technology services output, where demand has increased on the back of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption. The productivity trend also appears to be improving as growth in output per worker has increased significantly. At the same time, the worst of Brexit’s economic impact has probably passed, and survey data indicates that early gains from AI adoption could have started to modestly boost growth. “These factors, together with declines in energy prices, should mean that growth reaccelerates through the second half of next year,” Moberly and Stehn write. They also expect labor cost inflation to be well below the levels seen in recent years as a looser labor market reduces the extent to which higher headline inflation passes through into wage pressures. This should help to “keep a lid” on underlying services inflation despite pressures from higher food and energy prices, they write. Given their expectations of moderate second-round inflation effects from the energy shock, our economists think that the BoE will hike less than the market is pricing. “After tightening policy in February, we expect the Monetary Policy Committee to keep Bank Rate at 4.25% for the rest of the year, whereas the market implies two further rate increases,” they write. The UK government is also likely to make more progress on reducing its deficit in 2027, with a significant reduction planned. “Further consolidation should mean that the UK continues to compare favorably to other advanced economies in terms of reducing borrowing,” Moberly and Stehn write. This could in turn bring down borrowing costs. While next year’s Spending Review by the Office for Budget Responsibility poses a challenge for the government, it is possible that changes in the economic forecast could help the chancellor, Moberly and Stehn observe. The OBR’s wage growth forecast looks low, they write, and an upgrade would boost the tax revenues projection, increasing fiscal space. “We also see scope for sentiment around the UK’s longer-term economic prospects to improve,” Moberly and Stehn write. The UK’s specialization in high-value-added services makes it well-placed to benefit from AI adoption. Estimates from the International Monetary Fund indicate that a relatively high share of the UK workforce is exposed to AI, with a particularly large number of workers in roles that may see productivity gains but are less likely to be replaced by the technology. Survey data also suggests that firms expect adoption to result in sizable productivity increases in the coming years. And the UK is well-positioned in several high-growth innovative industries, including a world-leading position in life sciences such as pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, medical technology, and genomics, Moberly and Stehn note. Closer ties with the EU could provide another potential boost. The prime minister has indicated that he will outline options for how the relationship might develop following the upcoming summit. Those options might include a customs union, rejoining the single market, or even a second referendum on membership. Any reset would require negotiation, trade-offs, and time, Stehn and Moberly observe. “But it could bring significant economic upside, so signals towards improved trading links could start to lift optimism on the UK’s growth prospects,” they add. title: Former Rucsu GS leads sit-in demanding election schedule, Senate session - The Business Standard
content: Former Rajshahi University Central Students' Union (Rucsu) General Secretary Salahuddin Ammar led a sit-in organised by the Rajshahi University Reform Movement, demanding the announcement of the Rucsu election schedule and a Senate session. Some 15 to 20 students joined the programme, which began at 10:30am in front of the university's administrative building. They chanted various slogans demanding the Rucsu election and a Senate session. The protesters said Rucsu's tenure ended on 26 October, but the university administration had yet to take any visible initiative to announce the next election schedule. They described Rucsu as a democratic right of students and demanded that the administration announce the election schedule immediately. They vowed to continue the sit-in until the schedule was announced, adding that the administration must explain to the media why it could not announce the schedule if it failed to do so. Speaking at the programme, Salahuddin Ammar said the campus was currently peaceful and students from all political groups wanted Rucsu. "Everyone wants Rucsu. The administration must announce the election schedule as soon as possible. Our programme will continue," he said. Arif Alvi, member secretary of the Rajshahi University Reform Movement, said they would not tolerate any delay over Rucsu, accusing the administration of using the upcoming admission tests as a pretext to delay the election. "Rucsu is our right. Our movement will continue until the election is held," he said. Meanwhile, leaders and activists of the Rajshahi University chapter of Mancha-24 expressed solidarity with Salahuddin Ammar and the other protesters. title: GS Engineering & Construction Unveils AI Home for Residential Complexes - 조선일보
content: AI-powered homes with movable walls and enhanced security to debut in next-year projects GS Engineering & Construction has announced the future strategy for its residential brand “Xi,” stating that it will be applied to housing complexes scheduled for sale in the second half of next year. The core concept involves fully introducing an AI (artificial intelligence) system to create homes that understand residents’ lifestyles and operate autonomously. Walls are designed to be movable according to residents’ needs, providing flexibility in spatial configuration. GS Engineering & Construction held the Xi Future Strategy Presentation on the 16th at the Westin Seoul Parnas in Samseong-dong, Seoul. The company announced its brand strategy, which it has been pursuing for two years since overhauling the Xi brand for the first time in 22 years in 2024. The event was attended by GS Engineering & Construction executives, including Huh Yoon-hong, CEO of GS Engineering & Construction. The three core residential products prominently feature the ‘AI Home,’ jointly developed with LG Electronics. The AI Home provides an optimized living environment based on generative AI. Residents can issue voice commands as they normally speak, and the AI will control home appliances or adjust lighting. GS Engineering & Construction plans to advance the system to the point where AI can proactively identify residents’ needs. For example, gas valves will automatically shut off when children return home, and the system will detect emergencies indoors and alert external parties. This stage, which recognizes residents’ situations in real-time and autonomously executes necessary functions, is scheduled to be applied to housing complexes for sale in the second half of next year. The ‘IX Platform,’ which allows flexible rearrangement of indoor structures, will also be introduced. Based on smart prefab technology—where pre-fabricated structures are assembled on-site—walls can be moved according to situations and purposes, enabling changes to spatial layouts. The complex will also incorporate real-time detection systems and drainage/disaster prevention systems to respond to climate change, such as heatwaves and heavy rainfall. Meanwhile, GS Engineering & Construction apologized for a recent incident involving the leakage of residents’ personal information from an apartment community facility reservation and management system. In response to security-related questions about the AI system during the event, a source from GS Engineering & Construction stated, “Immediately after identifying the incident, we activated the crisis management committee to address it.” They added, “The AI Home applies motion sensors to detect human movement without using cameras, and we have strengthened security to prevent customer information leaks.”

title: GS E&C to Launch Level 3 AI Homes at Xi Complexes Next Year - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
Builder unveils "Beyond Living" vision at Xi future strategy event
Co-developed with LG Electronics, to debut with presales in November next year
IX platform aims to reshape interiors for longer-lasting homes
Redevelopment orders seen reaching 11 trillion won this year, a company record GS E&C held its Xi future strategy presentation, "RE:EVOLVE," at the Westin Seoul Parnas in Samseong-dong, Seoul, on the 16th, presenting "Beyond Living," a mid- to long-term vision to evolve in step with residents' lives and changes rather than remain merely a space called home. Huh Yoon-hong, chief executive of GS E&C, said in his opening remarks that the company "has constantly considered how to turn its promises for the future into reality," describing the event as the result. It marks the first concrete customer experience-centered brand strategy in the two years since the Xi rebranding in November 2024. The core elements are AI Home, the "IX Platform" that delivers variable space, and the "Clima System" that responds to climate change. AI Home, under joint development with LG Electronics, is a solution that integrates home appliances, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, residential facilities and lifestyle services into a single interface based on generative AI. Going beyond existing smart homes that operate devices on command, it aims to recognize residents' circumstances and execute needed functions first. AI reads the situation to control heating and cooling; operating costs remain a challenge GS E&C said it had defined the industry's first "Level of Housing Autonomy (LHA)" framework, which divides smart home technology into levels 0 through 5. Among these, Level 3 — "context-aware automation," which recognizes situations based on real-time information and adjusts lighting, temperature and ventilation — will be applied sequentially starting with complexes offered for sale in November next year. At the center of the connectivity is a ceiling-mounted built-in AI hub. It links lighting, heating, cooling and ventilation equipment as well as appliances and IoT devices. Switches are fitted with microphones and speakers so devices can be controlled by voice from anywhere in the home. The plan also envisions using conversation to access complex services such as checking parking locations and booking community facilities. Non-identifying sensors embedded in ceiling light fixtures detect occupancy and activity status without cameras. Planned functions include turning on lights, shutting the gas valve and sending a notification to a guardian when a child comes home, or adjusting lighting, temperature and humidity at bedtime. Ultimately the company is aiming for Level 5, in which the home judges and handles even exceptional situations on its own without the resident's instruction or approval. That, however, presupposes the completion of autonomous driving and artificial general intelligence (AGI) and an environment in which every household can use a humanoid robot. Lee Yong-koo, head of the division, put such an environment about five years away, saying, "The home must take on the role of integrated control of various devices and services." Privacy protection and the maintenance-fee burden that come with operating AI Home are challenges. GS E&C said it would process sensing information inside devices and run repetitive functions on a rules basis to cut the cost of external AI calls. Lee said, "If the tokens used for AI calls increase, it can translate into a burden on consumers, so we will handle repetitive functions on a rules basis to reduce costs." For voice information, some external transmission is unavoidable, but as data accumulates, repetitive patterns will be run on a rules basis, the company said. Nam Kyung-ho, head of GS E&C's architecture and housing business division, again apologized to customers over the leak of Xi community customer information. "We convened a crisis management committee, notified the relevant authorities and took follow-up measures," he said. "Since the introduction of AI Home means more customer information may be gathered, we will ensure thorough security." A home used for 50 to 60 years by changing its space — lowering life-cycle costs The IX Platform focuses on changing physical space. Based on smart prefab technology that assembles factory-made structures on site, it reduces structural constraints on interior space. Columns are placed outside the unit's interior space and movable walls are used, allowing space to be reconfigured across the life cycle — from single-person households to families with children and the elderly. The aim is long-life housing in which the frame lasts a long time while interior space is easily changed and repaired. Lee Yong-koo, head of GS E&C's architecture and housing design division, said long-life housing is generally based on a 50-year standard, adding, "On the premise that our precast concrete (PC) structure is used for 50 to 60 years, total life-cycle costs can be reduced." GS E&C said factory fabrication would cut on-site labor costs and construction periods while securing economic benefits from longer housing use. It did not, however, provide initial construction costs, the extent of any reduction in sale prices or specific cost-savings ratios. Movable walls will be pushed for application from next year, and the IX Platform's PC structure will undergo additional testing before being introduced sequentially in a pilot project in 2028. The Clima System comprises 31 climate-response solutions jointly researched with CRA, the design group led by architect Carlo Ratti. The concept is to detect environmental changes such as heat waves and torrential rain and activate facilities accordingly, linking drainage and disaster-prevention systems with rainwater recycling. Lee said the company is considering various approaches at each site, including heating and cooling using water from the adjacent Han River in the case of the Seongsu District 1 project. Redevelopment orders seen at 11 trillion won: "the largest since founding" Meanwhile, GS E&C, after winning the Seongsu District 1 redevelopment (2.154 trillion won), the Songpa Hanyang 2nd reconstruction (685.6 billion won) and the Seocho Jinheung reconstruction (679.3 billion won) this year, forecast that urban redevelopment orders would reach 11 trillion won by year-end. "Projects for which we have been selected as the contractor so far total about 5.5 trillion won, and we expect to win about another 5.5 trillion won in the remaining two months," Nam said. "It will be the largest since the company's founding." He added, "Next year's order target is 10 trillion won on an internal reporting basis, and it could be raised depending on market conditions." title: Even if people don't manipulate them one by one, artificial intelligence (AI) can control lighting a.. - 매일경제
content:
Even if people don't manipulate them one by one, artificial intelligence (AI) can control lighting and heating and cooling on its own, and if the family composition or lifestyle changes, an apartment can be shared again. GS Engineering & Construction unveiled "BEYOND LIVING," a mid- to long-term vision of residential brand Xi, and introduced three future residential products that apply artificial intelligence (AI), variable space, and climate response technologies, respectively. GS Engineering & Construction announced the plan at the "RE:VOLVE" presentation for the future strategy of Jai at Westin Seoul Parnas in Samseong-dong, Seoul on the 16th. The vision embodies the strategy pursued for about two years since the reorganization of the Zai brand in November 2024. If the existing apartment focused on the marketability at the time of moving in, such as location, design, and finishing materials, it is judged that the function of the house should also change in line with changes in the lives of residents in the future. The first axis, 'AI Home', is a system that links home appliances with residential facilities such as the Internet of Things (IoT), lighting, cooling, and ventilation based on Generative AI. If the existing smart home operated according to the conditions that the user ordered directly or set in advance, the AI home aims to execute the necessary functions by identifying the situation of the residents based on real-time data. To this end, GS E&C also established the "LHA" system, which divides the level of smart home technology into 0-5 levels, for the first time in the industry. Based on real-time data, this AI home aims to be at the level of "situation awareness automation" in the third stage (LV3) that recognizes residents and surrounding situations and judges and executes necessary functions on its own. For example, when a user says, "Please cool me down by the time I get home," AI calculates the location and expected return time and operates the cooling and lighting according to the arrival time. The plan is to raise the level of technology to predictive automation, which creates a necessary environment in advance by learning life patterns in the future. It also uses non-identification sensors instead of cameras to determine whether there are people in the house. It maintains lighting and temperature in human spaces and reduces energy use in empty spaces. GS E&C GS Engineering & Construction held “RE:EVOLVE,” a presentation on Xi’s future strategy, at the Westin Seoul Parnas in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, that day and unveiled future housing products incorporating artificial intelligence (AI), spatial innovation, and climate-response technologies. “BEYOND LIVING,” Xi’s mid- to long-term vision, embodies the goal of providing new experiences that reflect customers’ diverse lifestyles and changing needs, going beyond the physical value and functions of residential spaces. The vision gives concrete form to a customer-experience-centered brand strategy pursued for about two years since Xi’s brand was revamped in November 2024 for the first time in 22 years. Seo Aran, head of Brand Strategy at GS Engineering & Construction, said, “A new standard for residential brands means evolving in step with changes in people’s lives. We will create spaces that understand residents better the longer they live in them.” At the event, GS Engineering & Construction unveiled three key future housing products: “AI Home,” a home that understands residents’ lives and operates autonomously; the “IX Platform,” which allows spaces to be flexibly reconfigured according to each stage of life; and the “Clima System,” which actively responds to changes in the climate and environment. AI Home, which is being developed jointly with LG Electronics, is a solution that uses generative AI to integrate appliances, IoT devices, residential facilities, and lifestyle services through a single interface, providing residents with an optimized living environment. GS Engineering & Construction is the first in the industry to establish a housing autonomy level system (LHA) that divides the technological evolution of smart homes into six stages. The company is working to implement “context-aware automation (Level 3),” which uses real-time data to recognize residents’ circumstances and independently perform necessary functions. Residents can access a range of services inside and outside the home through natural conversations by voice or chat. Non-identifying sensors embedded in ceiling light fixtures recognize conditions such as whether someone is home and, based on residents’ lifestyle patterns, combine lighting, temperature, and ventilation settings to provide an optimal environment before residents even ask. Lee Yong-gu, head of the Architectural and Housing Design Division at GS Engineering & Construction, said, “AI Home has been applied on a trial basis at Mokdong Yoonseul Xi, which was offered for sale this year. We are developing a more complete system in cooperation with our technology research institute, and plan to apply it to residential complexes going on sale starting in the second half of 2027.” Regarding concerns about customer information leaks, Lee said, “To protect customers’ privacy, we decided to use only motion sensors instead of cameras. GS Engineering & Construction also unveiled related technologies as specific products under the IX Platform, including the “IX Slab,” which is lighter than a standard slab but enables longer spans; the “IX Wall,” a flexible space product that allows rooms to be freely repurposed; the “IX Switch Air,” which operates without a power source or battery; and “IX Lighting,” a next-generation lighting system that reproduces more than 95% of natural light. title: Global Stocks Are Expected to Rally in 2027 Even as Earnings Growth Slows - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Stock markets from New York to Tokyo are expected to extend their rally in 2027, even as earnings growth and investment in artificial intelligence (AI) slow in most regions, according to Goldman Sachs Research. What is the forecast for global stock market gains in 2027? The S&P 500 index of US stocks is predicted to produce a total return of 16% in the next 12 months (as of November 12). Europe’s STOXX 600 is expected to generate a total return of 13% in US dollar terms during that span, while Japan’s TOPIX is forecast to return 24%. In emerging markets, the MSCI EM index is projected to have a 21% total return. “We expect equities to generate positive returns, albeit with higher volatility than in recent years,” Peter Oppenheimer, chief global equity strategist and head of Macro Research in Europe, writes in a report. “We expect investors to seek companies that can sustain growth as it becomes more scarce.” Recent declines in equities mean stock valuations have come down substantially, particularly for technology companies, he writes. While nominal economic activity and earnings are predicted to grow at a slower pace in 2027, Goldman Sachs Research also projects inflation, bond yields, and oil prices will moderate. “We expect the equity bull market to continue,” writes Oppenheimer. On a risk-adjusted basis, Goldman Sachs Research favors overweighting US and Japanese stocks relative to a typical global benchmark and underweighting European stocks. Earnings growth rates are likely to at least halve in nearly all markets next year: US earnings growth is estimated to slow from 36% to 11%, Europe from just around 18% to 7%, Japan from 24% to 9%, and Asia from close to 80% down to less than 30%. One reason for the deceleration is slower growth in capex by hyperscalers, which is expected to result in a decline in earnings growth for AI infrastructure companies. In addition, energy prices are forecast to moderate, which will put pressure on that sector. How should investors allocate to their global stock portfolios in 2027? Goldman Sachs Research is focused on three key investment themes for global stocks in 2027: growth equities, selective defensive stocks, and companies that will benefit from lower oil prices and bond yields. “The expressions that best fit these themes vary somewhat across regions, and there is some overlap, particularly between defensive areas and bond beneficiaries,” Oppenheimer writes. Value companies that trade at a low price relative to fundamentals have outperformed faster-growing companies in recent months. But sharp rotations in performance have opened up value opportunities for investors in some technology companies, Oppenheimer writes. The price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio for technology stocks globally has fallen sharply both relative to its own history (it is now in the 20th percentile of its historical band over the past 20 years) and relative to other sectors. The information technology sector is now one of the cheapest on a P/E basis, and hyperscalers are cheaper than defensive areas of the market. Meanwhile the value factor, while cheaper in absolute terms, is close to the 90th percentile of its 20-year range and more expensive than growth relative to history. Oppenheimer says investors may find opportunities in US hyperscalers, power companies, and growth stocks. In Asia, he sees potential in Korean memory chipmakers as well as companies involved in optical networking, physical AI, and power. In Europe, opportunities may include technology, defense, and renewable energy stocks. There could be opportunities for defensive stocks, whose products are in demand even when economic growth slows. While Goldman Sachs Research expects resilient economic growth in 2027, the risks to that forecast are “skewed to the downside,” Oppenheimer writes. Slower growth in earnings per share, tighter financial conditions, elevated borrowing costs, and the risk of an earlier turn in the AI cycle indicate the potential need for portfolios with greater resilience. However, many of the traditional defensive stocks are no longer cheap. Goldman Sachs Research suggests a focus on defensive sectors that would also benefit from lower bond yields. Examples of companies that fit this criterion are utilities and telecoms in Europe; healthcare and companies consistently buying back their stock in the US; and Asian power companies. Financially strong “quality” companies should benefit from slower growth and tighter financial conditions, but it will remain important to be disciplined when it comes to valuations, Oppenheimer writes. High dispersion should create a better environment for stock-picking, with a focus on stable earnings, structural growth, strong balance sheets, and shareholder returns. Some stocks may benefit from lower energy prices and bond yields A recovery in energy supplies from the Persian Gulf should bring down commodity prices, including European gas prices, according to Goldman Sachs Research. Combined with fading US tariff effects and easing AI-related supply pressures, this should lower inflation and help central banks bring it back towards target, Oppenheimer writes. The US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank are expected to move towards rate cuts in late 2027, supporting modestly lower bond yields. Goldman Sachs Research’s rates forecasts remain more dovish than market pricing. Europe should be the clearest beneficiary of lower energy prices because of its greater exposure to imported energy and natural gas, according to Oppenheimer. He also sees opportunities in select US consumer companies, including consumer discretionary stocks and long-duration growth companies, whose profits are expected mostly in the distant future. title: CPIM is not a challenge for BJP; our challenge is to meet people’s expectations: Tripura BJP GS - India Today NE
content:
Tripura BJP General Secretary Chandan Debnath on Sunday, November 15 asserted that the Communist Party of India (Marxist) (CPIM) is not a political challenge for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), stating that the party’s real challenge is to fulfil the expectations of the people through continued development and good governance. Speaking about the political situation in Sonamura under Sepahijala district of Tripura and the upcoming municipal and civic body elections, Debnath said that the CPIM had attempted to create an atmosphere of fear and mistrust among minority communities by spreading misinformation about the BJP. He alleged that a section of people in Sonamura had been influenced by propaganda suggesting that under a BJP government, minorities would not be allowed to practise their religious traditions, including wearing caps and offering Azan. According to him, the party could not effectively counter this fear-driven campaign in Sonamura at the time.
 “CPIM is not a challenge for BJP. Our real challenge is to assess the work we have done over the last five years and identify how much more we can do for the people,” Debnath said. Reacting to the CPIM's criticism over the replacement of some former municipal representatives with new faces, Debnath defended the BJP's decision, saying that giving opportunities to new leaders is part of the party's approach to strengthening development-oriented governance. He questioned why the opposition was criticising the BJP for introducing new candidates when political leadership changes in every party over time. He also took a dig at the CPIM, saying that its leaders often make well-organised statements at press conferences, but their claims fail to stand before the people. Debnath further said that the BJP is committed to carrying forward Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of a 'Viksit Bharat' and supporting Chief Minister Professor Dr. Manik Saha's efforts to accelerate development in Tripura. He maintained that the BJP believes in bringing fresh leadership and new faces into public life to maintain the momentum of development, rather than allowing the same individuals to hold positions indefinitely.
Expressing confidence ahead of the upcoming civic body elections, Debnath said the BJP would focus on its development record, public outreach and commitment to addressing people's needs, rather than treating the CPIM as its principal electoral challenge. title: December closure of newsagent and Post Office leaves town asking what's next - The Western Telegraph
content:
The closure of a local newsagents and post office has left residents of a small west Wales town deeply saddened and worried about the future of its High Street. A wave of community support, sympathetic memories, and concerns for lost services was expressed on social media after the news that GS News in Newcastle Emlyn, which has been serving the market town for over two decades, will close on December 21. Readers commenting online picked up on the void that would soon be left in Newcastle Emlyn’s high street, especially as GS News has acted not only as a shop, but also as the town’s Post Office since 2015. GS News in Newcastle Emlyn will close next month after 21 years (Image: Google Street View) Comments combined nostalgia and gratitude to the shop for its service with anxiety about what such a loss means for residents and existing small businesses. Jacqueline Mary Byrne asked: “Are we to have a new Post Office?

  When the banks closed down we were told we could do banking transactions in the Post Office, where do we go now?” Readers recalled what GS News has meant for locals through thick and thin. Rebekah Davies posted about her morning paper round, helped along by Noel the postman when her car routinely broke down, and sent “all the best to everyone at GS News”. “Best wishes to all those staff and users affected and a big thank you to the owners for such great service over the years." Residents also worried about Newcastle Emlyn’s traditional high street disappearing. Joanne Elizabeth lamented, “Such a shame how Newcastle Emlyn is now a ghost town… it was a lovely busy little place." Bernie Bernie added, “The old Co-op shop is still shuttered, Bargain Box next door, also now closed, now GS News next to that. “Huge loss to Emlyn, all the banks closed down, now the post office, nowhere for businesses or people to conduct their financial business.” The feeling from many, including Huw Davies, was simply: “A very sad loss to Emlyn." Special gratitude was expressed to the shop’s staff. Sandra Bishop thanked "the ladies at the PO for the efficient and professional service they have provided. “Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi," she wrote adding that she hoped someone would take the shop over. Owner Sue Rogers, announcing the closure, said that she had hoped to keep the shop running following the sudden death of her husband Barry earlier this year. “I had very much hoped to be able to continue to keep the shop and Post Office open for the sake of the town and the townspeople,” she wrote in a post announcing the closure. “However, lately I have found it increasingly difficult physically to cope with the additional work and attendant stress, and now realise I simply have to slow down for my own well-being.” She added that she was currently in contact with the Post Office to discuss alternative accommodation for the service. title: A Dream Out of Reach... Gen.G's 7th Attempt Ends as Runner-Up - Inven Global
content: They came closer than ever on their seventh attempt, but in the end, it remained just out of reach. Gen.G Esports finished as runners-up after losing 1-3 to BLG in the finals of the 2026 LoL World Championship (Worlds), held on the 15th KST at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York. Though they reached the finals after seven attempts, they ultimately fell victim to BLG's championship narrative of knocking out LCK teams. Gen.G had made it to the Worlds stage without missing a single year since 2020, but the outcome was always cold. Despite consistently being named among the heavy favorites, they repeatedly failed to cross the semifinal threshold. Each time, they suffered unexpected defeats at the hands of different teams—G2, EDG, DRX, BLG, T1, and KT—forced to swallow the bitter pill of elimination. For Gen.G, the 2026 Worlds was a golden opportunity. Fitting for title contenders, they swept through the Swiss Stage with a 3-0 record, then shut out Lyon and IG in the quarterfinals and semifinals, respectively, reaching the finals for the first time in a very long while. However, victory once again eluded them. After winning the first game, they conceded three consecutive losses to BLG, settling for second place. Gen.G mid laner 'Chovy' also tasted the bitterness of defeat once more in his eighth attempt. Although he crafted a storyline of eight consecutive Worlds appearances and his first-ever final, his book remained unfinished once again. He had to watch his counterpart 'knight,' who had walked a similar path, lift the Summoner's Cup to bring a happy ending to his story. With this, Gen.G concluded their seventh attempt as their seventh failure. Though they were the most formidable force throughout the season, they were ultimately missing that final edge. As the saying goes, 'fall seven times, stand up eight'—leaving fans curious whether an eighth chance will come for Gen.G and what their next move will be.
